A nest for every bug, and a queen for each

You picked Earthworks: the nest digs outward as it grows. Each stage is its own drawing: one burrow at stage 1, a side burrow joined by a tunnel at stage 2, a dig site with five burrows and tunnels leaving the mound at stage 3.

This round adds runnels for runners and barrows for beetles, so each of the five bugs has its own nest. Each kind has a queen nest, and each bug has a queen.

Try the preview: it shows one nest at game scale with its blight. The dashed square marks the 2×2 tiles it blocks.

Five kinds, three stages, a queen nest each

Every kind shares the Earthworks growth: more burrows, tunnels, spoil and eggs at each stage, and scrap from your factory at stage 3. Each kind has its own soil and leftovers, so you can tell them apart from far off. A queen nest is wider and has a glowing royal chamber in the middle, with a ring of spikes in its bug’s colour.

The queens

Each queen is her bug with a swollen abdomen trailing behind, eggs showing through the skin, and a gold crest at the back of the head. Wasp queens keep the stripes and sting; beetle queens’ wing cases have split over the abdomen. They’re drawn in a box half again as big as a worker’s.

To settle before building it

Two new kinds and queen bugs change the rules as well as the art. These are my recommendations; tell me where you’d go another way.

Which bugs live where

Each kind is mostly its own bug, with some crawlers as now. Hives would hold wasps (with some runners) instead of runners, and dens brutes without beetles.

Distances follow today’s lines: warrens near the hub, runnels from 60 tiles, hives from 80, dens from 100, barrows from 120.

Queen nests

“Queen” stops being a kind of its own and becomes something any nest can be. A queen nest keeps today’s queen rules (3× mound health and chitin, breeds twice as fast, near the map edge) and its kind’s bugs.

Its kind comes from its distance like any nest. Today’s queen nests hold every bug kind; under this plan they’d hold only their own.

What a queen bug does

One queen lives in each queen nest. She stays in the chamber and comes out only once the mound falls, then fights as a slow, tough version of her bug (about 6× health, 2× bite).

Killing her drops extra chitin. While she lives, the nest’s bugs hatch faster. That’s already the queen nest’s rule, so it now has a face.

Saves

This changes saved state (nest kinds, the queen flag, queen bugs), so it needs a save version bump. Old queen nests become queen nests of their distance’s kind. Old hives and dens keep their bugs and only change the bugs they breed.

What it takes to put it in

  • Sprites: 5 kinds × 3 stages (nests/warren_1 … nests/barrow_3), 5 queen nests (nests/warren_queen …) and 5 queens (enemies/crawler_queen …), with walking strips for the queens. Hardcore gets a darker take on each stage instead of one nests/hardcore sprite.
  • Size: every stage drawn in the same 4-tile box (the Hardcore cover ring is 4×4 too); the art itself grows from about 1.6 tiles across to 3.4. The blocked 2×2 tiles don’t change.
  • Merged nests: stage 3 art at 1.3× as now, with a tunnel drawn in code towards each other cell the nest owns.
  • Kept as they are: the angry eyes, damaged rim and destroyed overlays, the health bar and the blight.
  • Done in steps: the art first (no rule changes: runners’ and beetles’ nests keep today’s kinds until the second step); then the two new kinds and the queen flag; then queen bugs.
